newsitem.title: USA: Northland purchase ended, sees earnings shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Northland purchase ended, sees earnings shortfall.

text.p: Northland Cranberries Inc said Thursday its pending acquisition of a private-label juice bottler and distributor was abruptly and unexpectedly terminated by the seller for undisclosed reasons.

"Because of the actions taken by Northland in anticipation that the acquisition would be completed in the near future, Northland expects to report substantially lower than expected fiscal 1997 earnings," the company said in a statement.
Northland said the reasons for terminating the transaction were apparently unrelated to Northland or the terms and conditions of the deal.
Northland declined to comment further on the identity of the seller or the proposed terms and conditions of the transaction.
Northland president and chief executive John Swendrowski said the company was considering its legal alternatives against the selling company and its shareholders.

Swendrowski said Northland had completed its due diligence and had received a firm bank financing commitment, an investment banking firm's fairness opinion and board of directors approval for the transaction and was preparing to sign the definitive purchase agreement when the sellers terminated the transaction.

"Based on our expectations that this deal would be consummated in the near future, we consciously took a number of actions to conserve our supply of cranberries and to delay our own entry into the private label cranberry juice market," Swendrowski said. "We obviously also incurred some substantial costs in negotiating and analyzing this acquisition."
He said the company is disappointed by the termination.

"We are shocked and disappointed by the sudden news that apparently we will not be able to complete a very attractive acquisition which would have immediately established Northland as a very significant supplier of private label cranberry juice products and allowed us to even more dramatically and quickly realize our 'marsh to market' strategic vision," Swendrowski said.
